title: Regulated degradation pass-through with per-model/dependency trip windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem summary: We need a predictable, auditable mechanism to degrade traffic when a model dependency or region crosses an operational safety threshold. Current binary trips (hard-cut) cause customer-facing errors or opaque 500s. Goal: implement a regulated "pass-through" degradation layer that applies staged actions (throttle, partial responses, model downgrade, cached reply) with per-entity trip windows (per-tenant, per-model, per-external-dependency) and hysteresis to avoid oscillation. This ticket covers design, prototype, and canary rollout for the runtime-side controller and the request router policy integration.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine supports 3 entity scopes: tenant, model (model-id), dependency (upstream-service-id)
Each scope can be configured with: trip metric (error-rate, spike-p95, cpu-saturation), trip threshold, minimum duration window, release/hysteresis window

When an entity trips, system applies staged actions in order: 1) request-shedding (probabilistic), 2) serve-from-prefetch/cache, 3) downgrade to a compatible quantized variant, 4) fail-open to a hosted fallback model with consistent headers
No production route should return an unhandled 500 because of a trip; instead responses should include X-Redwood-Degraded header with reason and action
Controller exposes metrics and events to the console and emits an incident event to the incident bus with full context
Canary rollout: changes deployed to 10% of hosts in eu-west-1 for 72h; observed SLOs must remain within 99% of baseline for unaffected tenants and show improved graceful survival for affected tenants
Unit and integration tests validating hysteresis (no oscillation for repetitive short spikes) and correctness of staged action ordering
Documentation and runbook published at the linked design doc
tasks: Design policy schema and default profiles for per-entity trip windows
Implement runtime controller: evaluation loop, state machine, and events
Integrate with request router to apply staged actions atomically
Expose metrics: trip_state, trip_reason, percent_shed, downgraded_model_id
Add header instrumentation and logging for degraded responses
Build canary: k8s manifests, feature flag gating, and monitoring dashboards
Write QA scenarios and chaos tests (packet loss, delayed responses, large fan-out)
Author docs + runbook and perform a tabletop exercise
design_decisions: Use probe-based trip detection: combine rolling-window error-rate with sudden-latency-spike detector to reduce false positives
Hysteresis implementation: enforce a minimum cool-down of 60s after an untrip before allowing re-enable; require 3 consecutive good windows to clear a trip
Staged actions are ordered by lowest customer-impact-first (probabilistic shed) to highest (model fallback) so we preserve availability where possible
Configuration tiers: global defaults, tier overrides (enterprise vs free), and per-tenant overrides stored in config service
Store trip state in distributed in-memory store with local caching and TTL to minimize router RPCs
tradeoffs_and_risks: Probabilistic shedding can increase tail-latency variance for those shed but preserves availability overall
Model downgrade preserves latency but may impact output quality — mitigated by tagging degraded responses and downstream quality monitoring
Prefetch/cache responses may leak stale content; we will limit cache-serving to short TTLs and only for idempotent requests

Storing state in the in-memory store reduces latency but introduces complexity for cross-region failover; cross-region sync will be eventual and we accept transient inconsistencies during global failover
Complex policy surface increases operational burden; we'll provide safe default profiles and a small set of supported knobs to start
implementation_notes: Controller will be a new process inside the runtime pod (controller binary) exposing a gRPC interface to the router
Evaluation cadence: sample windows of 15s with 1s bucketing for spike detection
Default thresholds: error-rate >= 2% over 1m OR p95 latency > 800ms for 3 consecutive windows triggers a trip
Probabilistic shed initial rate: linear ramp to 25% over 30s after trip; can be tuned per profile
Downgrade sequence must include capability negotiation: router checks compatibility table to find nearest compatible model variant
All degraded responses must include X-Redwood-Degraded: <scope>=<action> and X-Redwood-Trip-Reason headers for observability
qa_plan: Simulate dependency failure and assert staged actions fire in order and headers are present
Replay production traffic (redacted) under applied trip and validate no 500s are returned for affected tenant flows
Run chaos test where controller state store is partitioned and ensure routers fall back to safe defaults
Verify canary metrics and compare to baseline using the runtime SLI dashboard
rollout_plan: Merge feature flag guarded changes behind ff: regulated-degrade-v1
Deploy controller and router changes to staging; smoke test
Canary to 10% hosts in eu-west-1 for 72h with automated rollback on SLO regression > 1%
Gradual regional expansion: us-east-1, then ap-southeast-1 after 1 week of stable metrics
Open beta: opt-in tenants by config flag for one month before global default enablement
comments: 2025-10-08 — Marcus Nguyen: Initial spike analysis attached to design doc; leaning toward probe-based detection rather than purely rolling-error windows.
2025-10-15 — Eng lead (R. Thompson): Approve schema but require audit log events for every state transition (trip/clear) — added to implementation notes.
2025-10-29 — PM (Leah Ortiz): Customer groups flagged as high-risk must be able to opt-out of probabilistic shedding by default. Added per-tenant override path.
2025-11-05 — Security (N. Shah): Reviewed cache policy and requested TTL limits for cached degraded responses; noted encryption at rest for config store is required.
2025-11-12 — QA (I. Morales): Found oscillation in synthetic test when cool-down set to 30s; recommend 60s minimum — updated hysteresis decision.
2025-11-19 — Marcus Nguyen: Canary started in eu-west-1 (10% hosts). Early metrics show 18% of trips resolved to downgrade, 12% to probabilistic shed, no increased 5xxs so far. Will monitor for 72h.
